flagged.location: Obstacle-problem overview paragraph, clause beginning “the reaction is a nonnegative distribution”
flagged.evidence: The page says the reaction “vanishes on the noncontact set” without a continuity or representative convention. The obstacle definition imposes its inequality on almost-everywhere classes. The scoped complementarity corollary states this conclusion with the additional condition that “u and ψ have continuous representatives,” and Proof 1.2 uses that continuity to make {u>ψ} open. Without such a convention, the pointwise noncontact set is not canonical for general H¹ classes, nor is it specified as an open set on which the distribution vanishes.

flagged.location: Final paragraph, sentence beginning “Choice principles are inherited”
flagged.evidence: The page says “the explicit computations use only Countable Choice.” The current isoperimetric and obstacle examples assume AC and use the integration-by-parts supplier; that supplier’s Statement explicitly assumes both Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. The one-dimensional representative and trace suppliers also explicitly assume AC. These current example proofs therefore have choice footprints beyond Countable Choice.

The Statement gives no Countable Choice hypothesis, while Facts & Assumptions says “Given: Countable Choice” and [F7] says it is assumed for the measure and closure interfaces. Proof 3.1 selects a sequence of smooth approximants from the W₀¹,ᵖ closure. The cited W₀ definition begins “Assume Countable Choice,” and the cited linear-change-of-variables supplier also explicitly assumes it; the Statement does not discharge these prerequisites.
